size_pct_nav: 5 million shares, $289.431 million cost at year-end; just under 10% of bank, not 10% of Berkshire

drivers.driver: Reichardt and Hazen were outstanding, cost-conscious bank managers.
drivers.quote: the best managers in the business

drivers.driver: Buffett wanted well-managed banks at fair prices, not poorly managed banks merely because they were cheap.
drivers.quote: We have no interest in purchasing shares of a poorly-managed bank at a 'cheap' price.

drivers.driver: A severe California loan-loss stress could be absorbed by earning power without assuming a favorable economy.
Less than five times after-tax earnings supplied a substantial valuation cushion.

entry_valuation_stated: Buffett stated <5x after-tax and <3x pretax earnings for purchase window; exact October 24 quote not recovered.
outcome_note: Accumulation case, not lifetime P&L. About one-sixth of year-end position was bought in 1989 and the balance in 1990.
sources: Wells Fargo pre-cutoff operating facts reconstructed from Berkshire purchase discussion; https://www.nytimes.com/1990/10/25/business/company-news-buffett-acquires-9.8-of-wells-fargo-shares.html used only as archival chronology, not to reveal the stake; Los Angeles Times, July 18, 1990, https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1990-07-18-fi-684-story.html
pack_quality_notes: Rounded financial/stress anchors reconstructed from following-year explanation; original October regulatory schedules missing. New mode retained per assignment although this is accumulation. March 1 signing date is historical letter date, not claim of earliest disclosure.
